comment: The one source of truth for what changed in each release. Scripts/release.sh turns the matching entry into the appcast description Sparkle links to before installing, and into the GitHub release body. Newest first. A release with no entry here is refused by release.sh. By default an entry opens no window on launch — a fix does not earn an interruption. Add "showsWhatsNew": true for a release notable enough to announce itself, or "showsWelcome": true to show updating users the welcome window itself instead of these notes, for a release that changes how Perch introduces itself. Their existing settings are pre-filled, so the window changes nothing they do not change.

highlights.title: leave originals where they are
highlights.detail: a new switch under Advanced, Behavior lets Perch hold a pointer to each dropped file instead of moving it into its own storage. The existing move behavior stays the default.

highlights.title: quieter updates
highlights.detail: the update prompt is a small note with a link to the changelog instead of a wall of release notes, and perch no longer opens a window after every update — only after the rare release worth stopping for.

highlights.title: snapping while you drag
highlights.detail: pulling the shelf off its edge now offers the other edges — and the Dock, if you snap beside it — as you go, instead of only after you put it down and pick it up again.

versions.headline: Perch now tells you what changed.

highlights.title: What's New after an update
highlights.detail: Perch has no Dock or menu bar icon, so an update used to install and relaunch with nothing to show for it. Now it says what changed, once, and gets out of the way. Skip a few releases and you will see everything you missed.

highlights.title: Shake to summon is off by default
highlights.detail: It could fire during ordinary vigorous mouse movement, which is a surprising way to meet a feature you did not know existed. Turn it back on under Settings, Advanced. If you had already switched it on, it stays on.

versions.headline: The first launch now explains itself.

highlights.title: A welcome on first launch
highlights.detail: New installs get a short window explaining the two gestures Perch is built on, and Launch at Login is a checkbox you tick rather than a decision made for you.

highlights.title: Pick where the shelf lives
highlights.detail: Choose which screen edges it may use, then watch a shelf appear at every one of them at once. The notch is offered only on Macs that have one.

highlights.title: The shelf starts on the left
highlights.detail: New installs open on the left edge instead of the right.

highlights.title: ⌘-drag is discoverable
highlights.detail: The shelf could always be pulled off its edge to float anywhere, but nothing said so. Its menu now names the gesture, and stops once you have used it.
